title: Legacy AC2 and BR1 load DELEGATION_LIMIT through the reference-data service, but the Ownership Map keeps delegation_limit with P4 rwb-access
source: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (delegation_limit owner P4, asm ASM-A6-tables-4; reference_version, reference_row and lov_value owner P3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 043 Reference data service with versioned tables v2.md sections 7 AC2, 8 BR1 and 10; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 line 302
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules BR1; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.7 Tables owned
description: The preserved legacy story treats DELEGATION_LIMIT as one of the twelve reference tables that the reference-data service loads, versions and serves: AC2 loads it with 24 rows and BR1 lists it with the other eleven codes. The Ownership Map rules that the DoA table is P4 rwb-access (Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; ASM-A6-tables-4) while reference data stays with P3 (DP-07; ASM-A6-tables-5). Both readings cannot hold for one table: either the DoA table is duplicated in both services or the reference surface serves eleven of the twelve codes. The legacy AC text stays verbatim because the story is preserved, so the conflict is carried by this row and by the target reading in sections 3, 8 and 11 of RWB-P3-E1043-APP and in sections 2, 3, 8, 12.2 and 12.7 of RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
evidence: RWB-E1-043 section 7 AC2 (loads table DELEGATION_LIMIT with 24 rows), section 8 BR1 (twelve codes including DELEGATION_LIMIT), section 10 (approval of DELEGATION_LIMIT follows doa.txt rule 11); Ownership Map tables row delegation_limit with asm ASM-A6-tables-4 and ruling kept with P4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P4 REST GET /doa-limits) and slide 41 (P4 DoA table); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 line 302 (delegation limits held as versioned reference data)
proposed: Keep the legacy AC2 wording in the preserved story and apply the target reading: the reference surface of rwb-case serves the eleven non-DoA codes, a delegation limit is read from the rwb-access DoA operation GET /doa-limits declared in RWB-P3-E1043-CON section 12.2, and no copy of delegation_limit is created in rwb_case.

title: The column definitions of each reference table code and the element types of the reference resources have no source field by field
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 043 Reference data service with versioned tables v2.md sections 11, 12 and 13; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.2 reference_version and reference_row; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.23.3.2; RWB-P3-E1019-CON section 11
section: 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: (a) The legacy plan assumes that the column definitions per reference table code exist as data, but no source lists the columns, their types, their required flags or their key columns for any of the twelve codes. (b) The element types, lengths and required flags of the load, check-result and version-list resources that RWB-P3-E1043-CON publishes are not specified. (c) RWB-P3-E1019-CON already records that the remaining lov_value columns have no source, so the same gap runs through two stories of this service.
evidence: RWB-E1-043 section 13 build step 2 (build the column definitions per reference table code) and section 11 (field ids for reference_version, reference_row and the two lov_value fields only); TSD P3 v3 T3.2 lists the two tables field by field but no per-code column set; FSD P3 v4 A2.23 field catalog shows recovery_case columns and none of a reference table; RWB-P3-E1019-CON section 11 field identifiers with no source
proposed: Hold the per-code column definitions as data beside LOV-REF-TABLE and let the load row check read them; the contract publishes the resource element names of this key and leaves the types to the review with the data steward; the placeholder stays in sections 11 and 13 until the definitions are agreed.

title: The answer of a dated read with no version in force, and the rights of the verify and the rollback, are not stated
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 043 Reference data service with versioned tables v2.md sections 7 AC9, 10, 12 and 14; Ownership Map v1 sheet API (POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify and /rollback, asm ASM-A6-api-4)
section: 12.1 REST operations provided; 14 Validation and messages
description: (a) The legacy contract fixes 404 for an unknown load with MSG-P4-003, 409 for a duplicate valid from and 422 for a failed check, but it does not fix the answer of a read whose date has no approved version in force: AC9 fixes only the engine behaviour and the alert, and the as-built read is an in-process call with no HTTP answer. (b) The Ownership Map names the verify and the rollback operation of the reference load but no source gives the right each needs, while the legacy story gives C to the load and A to the approve.
evidence: RWB-E1-043 section 12 error rows (401 MSG-P4-001, 403 MSG-P4-002, 404 MSG-P4-003, 409 MSG-P3-027, 422 MSG-P3-027 or MSG-GEN-001); RWB-E1-043 section 7 AC9 and section 10 (Reference data C, A and R, RW-RISK approves); Ownership Map API rows for GET /admin/lists/{listCode}, POST /admin/reference-loads, .../verify, .../approve and .../rollback with no right column in any source
proposed: The dated read answers 404 with MSG-P3-027 naming the table code and the date and never an older version, a default row or an empty list; the verify and the rollback require Reference data A, the right the legacy story gives the approval, with the separation of duty of section 10 unchanged.
